problem.research_summary:
In characteristic zero, let a PCF conjugacy class on P1 have field of moduli K and trivial dynamical automorphism group. If its reduced postcritical set has odd cardinality, then the class has a K-defined representative. More generally, any finite conjugacy- and Galois-canonical set of odd cardinality splits the associated Brauer-Severi conic. The full odd-degree nonpolynomial PCF question remains unresolved in the literature verified during this run.

Candidate contribution (criterion; novelty confidence low): A rigid PCF conjugacy class with odd reduced postcritical cardinality is defined over its field of moduli; the same holds if any finite canonical portrait stratum has odd cardinality.

upstream_prior_report.problem:
The canonical record is **aim-dynamical-systems-notes.json**, zero-based index 81, from the AIM workshop *Postcritically finite maps in complex and arithmetic dynamics*, section “Moduli Problems,” problem 2.6. Its exact mathematical text is:

> field of definition vs field of moduli
>
> Are all PCF maps defined over their field of moduli?

The live AIM page was retrieved during this run and has the same wording, with no posted status or remarks. I interpret a “map” here in the standard dynamical-moduli sense: a \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\)-conjugacy class of degree-\(d\) rational self-maps of \(\mathbb P^1\), in characteristic zero. A field \(K\) is a field of definition when the class has at least one representative in \(K(z)\). This is different from asking whether a particular displayed formula has coefficients in \(K\).
upstream_prior_report.status_literature:
The complete PCF question was not resolved by the primary sources located in this run. The strongest verified general results are due to Silverman:

1. Every even-degree rational-map conjugacy class is defined over its field of moduli.
2. Every conjugacy class containing a polynomial is defined over its field of moduli, in every degree.
3. For every odd \(d\geq 3\), general nonpolynomial degree-\(d\) classes with trivial automorphism group can have a nontrivial field-of-moduli obstruction.

The first two assertions include classes with nontrivial automorphism group. Consequently every quadratic PCF map descends, as does every PCF polynomial. Silverman’s odd-degree counterexamples are not asserted to be PCF, and I did not find a primary source verifying a PCF counterexample. Thus the remaining part of the AIM question is the odd-degree nonpolynomial PCF locus, especially where the postcritical set has even cardinality or the map has nontrivial automorphisms.

A May 2024 arXiv abstract by Bresciani announces a complete characterization of descent for arbitrary dynamical systems on \(\mathbb P^1\). The abstract does not state a PCF corollary, and the paper PDF/source endpoints returned 404 during this run. No theorem from that unavailable text is used here.

Anderson--Bouw--Ejder--Girgin--Karemaker--Manes construct normalized dynamical Belyi maps. Their Proposition 2.3 gives a unique map over \(\mathbb Q\) for every genus-zero single-cycle type
\[
(d;e_1,e_2,e_3),\qquad 2\leq e_i\leq d,\qquad e_1+e_2+e_3=2d+1.
\]
These are useful explicit PCF test objects.
upstream_prior_report.work_done:
### 3. Definitions and assumptions

Let \(K\) be a characteristic-zero field with algebraic closure \(\overline K\), and let
\[
\phi:\mathbb P^1_{\overline K}\longrightarrow\mathbb P^1_{\overline K},
\qquad \deg\phi=d\geq2.
\]

- The dynamical automorphism group is
  \[
  \operatorname{Aut}(\phi)=
  \{h\in\operatorname{PGL}_2(\overline K):h^{-1}\phi h=\phi\}.
  \]
- The field of moduli of \([\phi]\) is \(K\) when every \(\sigma\in G_K\) sends \(\phi\) to a conjugate and \(K\) is the corresponding fixed field.
- The critical set is the support of the ramification divisor. The reduced postcritical set is
  \[
  P_\phi=\bigcup_{n\geq1}\phi^n(\operatorname{Crit}(\phi)).
  \]
  The map is PCF precisely when \(P_\phi\) is finite.
- A finite reduced set \(S_\phi\subset\mathbb P^1(\overline K)\) is called *canonical for conjugacy and Galois* if
  \[
  S_{h^{-1}\phi h}=h^{-1}S_\phi,\qquad
  S_{{}^{\sigma}\phi}={}^{\sigma}S_\phi .
  \]
  The postcritical set is canonical in this sense.

The main new criterion below assumes \(\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)=1\). This hypothesis is not cosmetic: only then are the Galois conjugators unique and hence an honest \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\)-cocycle.

### 4. Approach map

The descent obstruction can be viewed in four equivalent ways in the trivial-automorphism case:

\[
\text{Galois conjugators}
\longrightarrow H^1(K,\operatorname{PGL}_2)
\longrightarrow \text{Brauer--Severi conic }X/K
\longrightarrow \operatorname{Br}(K)[2].
\]

The class descends to a \(K\)-model on \(\mathbb P^1\) exactly when the conic \(X\) has a \(K\)-point. The strategy is therefore to transport canonical dynamical data from \(\mathbb P^1_{\overline K}\) to \(X_{\overline K}\). An odd-degree invariant divisor on \(X\) forces \(X(K)\neq\varnothing\). For a PCF map, the reduced postcritical set supplies just such a divisor when its cardinality is odd.

### 7. Detailed proof, derivation, or heuristic

#### 7.1 The cocycle and the conic

For each \(\sigma\in G_K\), choose \(f_\sigma\in\operatorname{PGL}_2(\overline K)\) satisfying
\[
{}^\sigma\phi=f_\sigma^{-1}\phi f_\sigma.
\]
When \(\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)=1\), \(f_\sigma\) is unique. Comparing the equations for
\(\sigma\), \(\tau\), and \(\sigma\tau\) gives the cocycle relation
\[
f_{\sigma\tau}=f_\sigma\,{}^\sigma f_\tau
\]
for the left Galois-action convention. Hence \(f=(f_\sigma)\) defines
\[
c_\phi\in H^1(G_K,\operatorname{PGL}_2).
\]

The corresponding twist of \(\mathbb P^1\) is a Brauer--Severi conic \(X/K\). There are an
\(\overline K\)-isomorphism
\[
i:\mathbb P^1_{\overline K}\overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow}X_{\overline K}
\]
and a \(K\)-morphism \(\Phi:X\to X\) with \(i\phi=\Phi i\). Silverman proves
\[
[\phi]\text{ has a }K\text{-model}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
X(K)\neq\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
c_\phi=1.
\]

#### 7.2 Why a canonical finite set descends

With the standard descent convention, \({}^\sigma i=i\circ f_\sigma\). Canonicity gives
\[
{}^\sigma S_\phi
=S_{{}^\sigma\phi}
=S_{f_\sigma^{-1}\phi f_\sigma}
=f_\sigma^{-1}S_\phi.
\]
Let
\[
D_S=i_*\left(\sum_{p\in S_\phi}[p]\right)
\]
on \(X_{\overline K}\). Then
\[
{}^\sigma D_S
=({}^\sigma i)_*\left(\sum_{p\in{}^\sigma S_\phi}[p]\right)
=(i f_\sigma)_*
 \left(\sum_{p\in f_\sigma^{-1}S_\phi}[p]\right)
=D_S.
\]
Thus \(D_S\) is a \(K\)-rational divisor on \(X\), and
\(\deg D_S=\#S_\phi\).

#### 7.3 Odd degree splits a conic

The index of a conic divides \(2\), since the anticanonical class gives a rational divisor of degree \(2\). It also divides the degree of every \(K\)-rational divisor. If \(\deg D_S\) is odd, then
\[
\operatorname{ind}(X)\mid\gcd(2,\deg D_S)=1.
\]
Therefore \(\operatorname{ind}(X)=1\). For a conic, index one is equivalent to a \(K\)-point, so \(X\simeq_K\mathbb P^1\). Transporting \(\Phi\) along this \(K\)-isomorphism produces a rational map in \(K(z)\) conjugate to \(\phi\). This proves the theorem.

Taking \(S_\phi=P_\phi\) proves the PCF corollary: ramification and iteration commute with both Galois action and conjugation, so \(P_\phi\) is canonical, and PCF makes it finite.

#### 7.4 The \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\) versus \(\operatorname{GL}_2\) audit

Choose arbitrary matrix lifts \(F_\sigma\in\operatorname{GL}_2(\overline K)\) of \(f_\sigma\).
The projective cocycle identity says
\[
F_\sigma\,{}^\sigma F_\tau\,F_{\sigma\tau}^{-1}
=a_{\sigma,\tau}I
\]
for scalars \(a_{\sigma,\tau}\in\overline K^\times\). Their class lies in
\[
H^2(G_K,\overline K^\times)=\operatorname{Br}(K)
\]
and is \(2\)-torsion; it is the quaternion/conic obstruction. Hilbert 90 applies to an actual
\(\operatorname{GL}_2\)-cocycle, not directly to \(f_\sigma\). The odd divisor proves that this
Brauer class vanishes; after scalar adjustment, Hilbert 90 supplies the desired coordinate change.
Thus the proof does not incorrectly lift a projective cocycle for free.

#### 7.5 A genuinely odd-degree nonpolynomial PCF test class

Consider the abstract single-cycle Belyi type
\[
(d;e_1,e_2,e_3)=(7;4,5,6).
\]
The relation \(4+5+6=2\cdot7+1\) meets the genus-zero condition. By Anderson et al.,
there is a unique normalized map \(f\in\mathbb Q(z)\) of this type. Its only critical points are
\(0,1,\infty\), they are fixed, and their local degrees are \(4,5,6\). Hence
\[
P_f=\{0,1,\infty\},\qquad \#P_f=3.
\]
Any dynamical automorphism must permute critical points while preserving local degree. Since
\(4,5,6\) are distinct, it fixes all three points and is the identity. No point is totally ramified
(local degree \(7\)), so the class is not polynomial. This gives a concrete odd-degree,
nonpolynomial, rigid PCF class to which the criterion applies.

This example is already defined over \(\mathbb Q\); it is a test of the scope of the criterion,
not a counterexample to the AIM question.

### 8. Verification and attempted falsification

1. **Functoriality check.** If \(\psi=h^{-1}\phi h\), then
   \(\operatorname{Crit}(\psi)=h^{-1}\operatorname{Crit}(\phi)\) with matching local degrees,
   and induction gives \(P_\psi=h^{-1}P_\phi\).
2. **Multiplicity check.** The theorem uses the reduced postcritical divisor, so its degree is
   exactly \(\#P_\phi\). Collisions of critical orbits are intentionally counted once.
3. **Parity check.** The ramification divisor has degree \(2d-2\), always even. Therefore merely
   knowing that critical orbits are finite does not force a split conic. This identifies the exact
   gap in the tempting argument “PCF supplies a divisor, hence descent.”
4. **Even-degree consistency.** The fixed-point divisor has degree \(d+1\). For even \(d\) this is
   odd, recovering Silverman’s conic argument in the trivial-automorphism case.
5. **Automorphism check.** If \(\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)\neq1\), the conjugator \(f_\sigma\) is
   defined only modulo \(\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)\), and
   \(f_\sigma{}^\sigma f_\tau f_{\sigma\tau}^{-1}\) may be a non-scalar dynamical automorphism.
   The asserted canonical conic is then unavailable without an additional lifting argument.
6. **Boundary check.** The proof is stated in characteristic zero. In positive characteristic,
   inseparability and wild automorphisms require separate hypotheses.

No heavy computation was used.
upstream_prior_report.result:
### 5. Main result

#### Theorem (odd canonical-divisor descent criterion)

Let \(K\) have characteristic zero, let \([\phi]\) have field of moduli \(K\), and assume
\(\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)=1\). Suppose \(S_\phi\) is a finite canonical reduced set for conjugacy and Galois. If
\[
\#S_\phi\quad\text{is odd},
\]
then \(K\) is a field of definition for \([\phi]\).

#### PCF corollary

If \(\phi\) is PCF, \(\operatorname{Aut}(\phi)=1\), and
\[
\#P_\phi\equiv1\pmod 2,
\]
then \([\phi]\) is defined over its field of moduli.

More generally, the same conclusion holds if any conjugacy-covariant portrait stratum (or invariant union of such strata) is finite and has odd cardinality. Examples include sets specified intrinsically by exact preperiod, period, and local ramification data.

#### Previously known automatic cases

Independently of the automorphism group and independently of PCF:

- if \(d\) is even, the fixed-point divisor has odd degree \(d+1\), and descent holds;
- if the class contains a polynomial, descent holds.

The PCF corollary is therefore useful principally for odd-degree nonpolynomial classes.

### 6. Candidate novel contribution

**Candidate claim.** A rigid PCF conjugacy class with odd reduced postcritical cardinality is defined over its field of moduli; more generally, any odd finite canonical portrait divisor kills the Brauer--Severi obstruction.

**Scope.** Characteristic zero, rational self-maps of \(\mathbb P^1\), and trivial dynamical automorphism group. For marked portraits, the same argument applies when the marked object has trivial automorphism group.

**Why it may be new.** Silverman explicitly applies the odd-divisor mechanism to the fixed-point divisor of degree \(d+1\), but the PCF postcritical divisor and portrait-stratum formulation were not located in the literature checked. The argument is short and close to Silverman’s method, so it may be known implicitly.

**Literature checked.** Silverman’s 1995 paper; the AIM source page; Anderson et al. on dynamical Belyi maps; targeted searches for “postcritically finite field of moduli field of definition,” “PCF maps field of moduli,” and related pseudoreal/descent terms. A 2024 abstract announcing a general characterization was found but its text was unavailable.

**Novelty confidence:** low.
upstream_prior_report.what_remains:
### 9. Limitations and unresolved gaps

- This does not answer whether *all* odd-degree nonpolynomial PCF maps descend.
- It says nothing when \(\#P_\phi\) is even and no other canonical odd divisor is available.
- It does not handle a nontrivial dynamical automorphism group. Silverman can handle all
  automorphism groups for even degree and polynomial classes, but the present PCF parity proof
  cannot simply be copied to the remaining cases.
- No verified odd-degree PCF counterexample was found. Silverman’s general counterexamples
  cannot be called PCF without a separate orbit computation.
- The literature search was not exhaustive, and the inaccessible 2024 preprint may contain a
  characterization relevant to the residual cases.

#### Marked versus unmarked objects

A map with marked critical/postcritical data is a different moduli problem. Its field of moduli
may be larger than that of the unmarked conjugacy class. If the marked object has trivial
automorphism group, the same cocycle construction applies. A Galois-compatible marked point
then becomes a \(K\)-point of the obstruction conic and forces descent immediately. Without
rigidity, descent is a gerbe/automorphism problem, not automatically a single conic problem.

### 10. Concrete next steps

1. Recover and verify the theorem statements in Bresciani’s 2024 preprint, then specialize its
   characterization to PCF portrait strata.
2. Search odd-degree PCF databases, beginning with cubic nonpolynomial maps, for classes with
   even \(\#P_\phi\). Compute their automorphism groups and the associated conic when the group is
   trivial.
3. For a candidate class over a quadratic extension \(L/K\), solve
   \({}^\tau\phi=f^{-1}\phi f\), verify \(f\,{}^\tau f=1\) in
   \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\), and test the associated norm/quaternion class.
4. Develop a version for nontrivial automorphism groups by marking enough portrait data to
   rigidify, while tracking how the marked field of moduli compares with the unmarked one.

### References

1. Joseph H. Silverman, “The field of definition for dynamical systems on
   \(\mathbb P^1\),” *Compositio Mathematica* **98** (1995), 269--304.
   https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1995__98_3_269_0/
2. Jacqueline Anderson, Irene Bouw, Ozlem Ejder, Neslihan Girgin, Valentijn Karemaker,
   and Michelle Manes, “Dynamical Belyi maps,” arXiv:1703.08563v2 (2017).
   https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.08563
3. Giulio Bresciani, “Fields of definition of dynamical systems on
   \(\mathbb P^1\). Improvements on a result of Silverman,” arXiv:2405.03612v2 (2024),
   abstract only verified in this run. https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.03612
4. AIM Problem Lists, “Postcritically finite maps in complex and arithmetic dynamics:
   Moduli Problems,” problem 2.6. http://aimpl.org/finitedynamics/2/
